newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: RTRS-Papua New Guinea 1995/96 coffee exports rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Papua New Guinea 1995/96 coffee exports rise.

text.p: Papua New Guinea's coffee exports rose to 1.13 million 60-kg bags in the 1995/96 season ended September 30 from 1.03 million in 1994/95, the PNG Coffee Industry Corp Ltd reported on Wednesday.

The corporation roughly estimated that coffee production rose to 1.1 million bags in 1995/96 from 969,000 bags in 1994/95 but many factories had not as yet submitted production data, it said in its latest bulletin.
The 1995/96 coffee year was the fourth year in a row that exports exceeded the one million bag mark, chief executive Ron Ganarafo said in the bulletin.

Ganarafo said that even though coffee production estimates were not available due to lack of cooperation from factories, the export figures were a good reflection of production, given that PNG does not carry large stocks from one year to another.
Given that there has no real new planting in PNG, it seems that with good rehabilitation and crop husbandry, the existing tree stock has the potential to produce at least 1.2 million bags, he said.
"With new plantings, the production target of two million bags by year 2007 is not that difficult to achieve," he said.
The corporation said the bulk of 1995/96 coffee exports - 57.4 percent - were destined for German ports.
Australia (20 percent of exports), the United States (6.7 percent), Britain (6.0 percent) and New Zealand (2.2 percent) were the other major markets, it said.
Of PNG's total coffee exports in 1995/96, 95.5 percent was Arabica and 4.5 percent Robusta, it said.
The value of PNG's coffee exports fell to 207.41 million kina (US$152 million) in 1995/96 from 246.51 million in 1994/95, reflecting lower prices, it said.
